raw.comments: Work in Global mode but restrict the actual edit to Tablet/DecidingFront.tex and any import needed by its existing support; preserve the Lean theorem statement and do not change target claims or add helpers. The current proof is only an outline. Cite DecidingFrontSet, DecidingPrefix, LocallyConstant, ProperPrefixSet, ProperInitialSegment, InitialSegment, Front, and FrontBase at their uses. First, from local constancy at an increasing enumeration x with witness n, define the finite set of the first n values of x, prove it is a proper-prefix set of range(x), and prove that any two increasing enumerations having that same finite-set prefix agree coordinatewise through n, so DecidingPrefix follows. For density, start with an arbitrary infinite Y subset of the base, obtain or explicitly construct an increasing enumeration with range Y, and show that repeatedly removing a proper deciding initial segment stays on that branch and terminates because the finite cardinality strictly decreases; the terminal set satisfies exactly the DecidingFrontSet minimality condition. Prove prefix-freeness by applying that minimality to two front members in the InitialSegment relation. Handle the constant case completely: empty is deciding, every nonempty deciding prefix has empty as a proper initial segment, and therefore the front is exactly {empty}. In the nonconstant case prove empty is not deciding; for each n use a branch beginning with n, obtain a nonempty minimal prefix on that branch, and unpack ProperPrefixSet to show n belongs to it, yielding FrontBase equal to the universal base. Finally explicitly discharge the infinite-base and dense fields of the Lean Front structure, rather than referring to three clauses informally. The paper construction at lines 1277-1287 is the source route. If using InfiniteSetEnumeration for arbitrary infinite bases, add its honest import and citation.
